Team — quick legal view based on what you've outlined:

1) UK customers: recommended path is UK IDTA (or the UK Addendum to the SCCs) when processing involves UK-resident data. The UK regulator expects explicit UK-specific documentation; relying solely on EU SCCs increases friction with procurement.

2) SCCs + TIA: for EU->US processing we should pair the SCCs with a Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) that documents the residual risks and supplemental safeguards (encryption, limited access, logging). That combination meets most enterprise procurement bar.

3) Practical approach: produce three artifacts for Zenos procurement — (a) SCCs + signed annex, (b) TIA summary (one-page executive + technical appendix), and (c) a UK Addendum (if UK-resident data is in scope).

4) Contract redlines: I can prepare a short redline pack that retains Redwood’s standard security commitments but adds the requested evidence delivery SLAs (e.g., SOC 2 snapshot within 5 business days, subprocessor list updates monthly).

I'll attach a short note with recommended language and a checklist. Happy to join the sync.

Regards,
Emma Harrison
Partner — Data Privacy & Security
Harrison & Co.
